# Getting started

This page shows the runtime API. To create the font data, see
[converter.md](converter.md).

## Basic drawing

TinyFonts renders into any target that implements `tinyfonts::FontDisplay`.
The target receives one call per pixel with a coverage value from 0 (no ink)
to 255 (full ink) and blends it with the background itself.

```cpp
#include <TinyFonts.h>
#include <TinyFonts/Fonts/Lato12.h>             // bundled, or generated by tools/tinyfonts_convert.py

class MyDisplay : public tinyfonts::FontDisplay {
 public:
  void drawPixel(int x, int y, uint8_t coverage) override {
    // blend `coverage` with the background and write the pixel
  }
};

MyDisplay display;
tinyfonts::TextRenderer text(Lato12, display);

text.drawText(0, 0, "Hello, TinyFonts!");            // \n starts a new line
text.drawText(0, 40, "A longer paragraph ...", 120);  // wrapped to 120 px
```

`drawText(x, y, text, maxWidth)` puts the top-left corner of the first line at
`(x, y)`. The baseline sits `ascent` pixels below it. `maxWidth <= 0` disables
wrapping. The function returns a `tinyfonts::TextBox` with the drawn width,
height and line count.

## Measuring text

```cpp
const char* s = "Grüße";
tinyfonts::TextBox box = tinyfonts::measureText(Lato12, s, s + strlen(s), 120);
// box.width, box.height, box.lines
```

## Clipping

```cpp
text.setClip(0, 0, 120, 60);   // draw only inside [0,120) x [0,60)
text.clearClip();
```

## Lower-level helpers

- `tinyfonts::decodeUtf8(p, end)` decodes one UTF-8 character and advances `p`.
- `tinyfonts::wrapText(font, begin, end, maxWidth, onLine)` calls `onLine` for
  each wrapped line.
- `tinyfonts::findGlyph`, `tinyfonts::kerning` and `tinyfonts::Font` expose
  the font data directly. See [format.md](format.md).

## Fonts in flash

Generated fonts are `PROGMEM` arrays with a `tinyfonts::Font` object. On AVR
and ESP8266 the library reads them from flash automatically. On other boards
they are ordinary constant data.

## Features and limits

- Coverage depth of 1, 2, 4 or 8 bits per pixel (anti-aliasing).
- Proportional advances, pair kerning from the `kern` and GPOS tables.
- Ascent, descent and line gap; `\n` line breaks.
- Word wrapping. Words that are too long are split between characters.
- UTF-8 input. Characters the font lacks are drawn with the fallback glyph.
- Clipping rectangle.
- Not implemented yet: TrueType/CFF outline rendering, signed distance fields,
  colour glyphs, complex text shaping (ligatures, Indic scripts) and font
  fallback chains.
